title: Sooryavanshi's 93 Off 38 Balls Blows Away LSG and Sends Rajasthan Royals Storming Into Fourth. Pant Drops an F-Bomb on Live TV.
excerpt: The 15-year-old from Bihar became the youngest batter to reach 500 IPL runs in a season, broke Andre Russell's strike-rate record, and made a 221-run chase look routine. For NRIs glued to late-night streams, this kid is the reason you set the alarm.
body:
The run-chase looked improbable on paper. Lucknow Super Giants had just posted 220 for 5 — powered by Mitchell Marsh's belligerent 96 off 57 and Josh Inglis's 60 — on a batting paradise at Sawai Mansingh Stadium in Jaipur. Rajasthan Royals, without injured skipper Riyan Parag, needed their biggest chase of the season to keep playoff hopes alive.

They got it, and then some. A 15-year-old made it look like a backyard game.

## The Sooryavanshi Show

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi walked in with RR needing 221 and proceeded to play one of the most extraordinary innings in IPL history. Starting cautiously at 5 off 10, the left-hander from Bihar flicked a switch. His fifty came up off 23 deliveries. From there, he plundered 42 more runs off just 13 balls before Mohsin Khan finally ended the carnage at 93 off 38 — 10 sixes, 7 fours, and a strike rate that beggared belief.

In the process, Sooryavanshi crossed 500 runs for the season in his 13th match, overtaking Rishabh Pant's 2018 effort for then-Delhi Daredevils to become the youngest batter ever to reach that landmark in an IPL campaign. His season strike rate of 236.32 now tops every 500-plus season in IPL history — Andre Russell's explosive 2019 (205.0) included. With 53 sixes, he also leads the season charts.

And he is fifteen.

His 105-run partnership with the more measured Dhruv Jurel (53 not out off 37) took the game away from LSG entirely. Stand-in captain Yashasvi Jaiswal contributed a brisk 43 at the top, and Donovan Ferreira's late cameo sealed the deal in 19.1 overs. Final score: 225 for 3.

## LSG's Season of Pain

For Lucknow, it was defeat number nine in thirteen matches — and the most bruising kind, the sort where you put up 220 and still lose by seven wickets with five balls to spare. Mitchell Marsh, run out for the second consecutive match in the nineties, was left stranded again. Josh Inglis had given them a platform. Pant himself chipped in with 35. It still was not enough.

After the match, the LSG skipper did not mince words. Rishabh Pant told the post-match broadcast — on national television — that his side remains "a f***ing good team," frustration boiling through an otherwise composed assessment. He acknowledged the difficulty of defending totals on flat surfaces but insisted the squad's belief has not wavered.

"Results do not define our internal confidence," Pant said. "We could have scored five or ten runs more with that kind of start. We just couldn't capitalise."

It was the kind of raw honesty that has defined Pant's career — the same instinctive candour that endeared him to fans worldwide during his extraordinary comeback from a near-fatal car crash in December 2022. But candour alone will not salvage an IPL season that has yielded four wins from thirteen outings and a net run rate of -0.702.

## What This Means for the Playoff Race

With this result, Rajasthan Royals jump to fourth with 14 points, leapfrogging Punjab Kings (13 points, five consecutive losses) and giving themselves a genuine shot at the knockouts. RCB remain on top with 18, Gujarat Titans and Sunrisers Hyderabad occupy second and third with 16 apiece, and below the Royals, five teams between 11 and 13 points are still mathematically alive with six matches remaining.

LSG, at 8 points with just one match left, are playing for pride alone.

## The NRI Watch Party

For diaspora cricket fans who have been setting alarms for JioHotstar streams or juggling Willow TV subscriptions to catch the IPL's business end, Sooryavanshi has become the compelling reason to stay up. At 15, he is not just an IPL story — he is a generational talent announcing himself to the world. In living rooms across New Jersey, Brampton, and Birmingham, the conversation has shifted from "Who replaces Kohli?" to "How do you plan for a teenager who hits sixes like he's playing gully cricket?"

The boy from Samastipur, Bihar — population under 100,000 — is rewriting record books that were supposed to belong to grown men.

The IPL playoffs begin on May 26 with Qualifier 1 in Dharamsala. If Sooryavanshi keeps this up, the Rajasthan Royals might just have the most dangerous weapon in the tournament.
